description: Eight-voice algorithmic sequence generator: instead of programming notes you pick the scale and set the algorithm, and it produces eight note CVs and gates plus four modulation CVs and gates

params.text: Steps the scale selection on each press, from scale A to scale B to both scales stacked an octave apart and back
Raises every note taken from scale A by one octave
Raises every note taken from scale B by one octave
While this is on, changing the scale A preset overwrites the twelve note buttons of scale A; turn it off to keep edits you make by hand
While this is on, changing the scale B preset overwrites the twelve note buttons of scale B; turn it off to keep edits you make by hand
Picks one of sixteen five-note presets for scale A, stepping from 1 to 16; it changes nothing until the preset switch beside it is on
Picks one of sixteen five-note presets for scale B, stepping from 1 to 16; it changes nothing until the preset switch beside it is on
Sets the internal clock, from 32 BPM at the left to 2048 BPM at the right; it has no effect while a cable is in the clock input
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before it wraps and fires the reset output, 1 to 64
Transposes every note CV, -3V to +3V at a volt per octave
Sets the note gate length as a fraction of one step, 0.01 to 2, so a setting of 1 holds the gate for a whole step; the maker's tooltip prints the value in seconds
Sets how many of the eight voices produce gates, 1 to 8; the note CV outputs above the count keep moving but their gates stay low
Delays each voice's gate a little further than the one before it, spreading a chord into a strum across up to one step
Sets the divisors and phases of the eight internal tracks whose on and off states the notes are built from, stepping from 0 to 127
Picks which of the eight internal tracks feed each voice's note and which of sixteen gate patterns is used, stepping from 0 to 127
Steps each voice along the scale by this many notes, 0 to 12; above 6 each voice is shifted one step further than the one before it, fanning the voices apart
Sets how often a voice is silenced and for how many steps, 0 to 16, thinning the sequence as it is raised
Reads each voice further back through the last eight steps, -8 to +8, so the voices play the same material against itself in time
Feeds the module's own note CV outputs back into its algorithm controls, 0 to 127; the higher it goes the more controls it reaches
Puts that note into scale A, or takes it out; the generator picks only from the notes that are in
Puts that note into scale B, or takes it out; the generator picks only from the notes that are in

A 1ms 10V pulse each time the sequence wraps round to its first step, and on every reset

notes: the module runs on its own clock until a cable is patched into the clock input, at which point the SPEED knob stops mattering and each rising edge is one step.
the note buttons are the scale: with no note switched on in the selected scale every gate stays low and every note CV holds at one value.
a preset switch left on overwrites the note buttons of its scale every time the preset changes, including when its CV moves. Switch it off after choosing a preset to keep edits made by hand.
the two polyphonic modulation jacks carry eight channels each, although only four of the modulation voices have a jack of their own.
six of the controls are only read on a step: the voice count, the two algorithm values, the shift, the space and the rotation. Turning one takes effect at the next clock, not at once.
note CVs are clamped to plus or minus 10V, so patching a note output back into the transposition input cannot run away.
the eight modulation CVs and gates are built from the same eight internal tracks the notes are, so they move in step with the sequence rather than independently of it.
